results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing Explained: On-Demand, Reserved, Bare Metal
highlights:
- On-demand buys flexibility: You pay per GPU-hour with no commitment and can stop at any time, which suits experiments, bursty jobs, and workloads whose utilization you have not measured yet.
- Reserved pricing buys a lower rate: Committing to a term lowers the effective hourly price, but you pay for every hour of the term, so it only saves money when utilization stays above the break-even point set by the discount.
- Bare metal is a deployment model, not a billing term: It gives you the whole physical server with root access and no hypervisor, which can be bought on demand or reserved, and NVIDIA has measured virtualized training running 12% slower than bare metal.
- Published rates are only a starting point: On GMI Cloud, on-demand rates start at $2.60 per GPU-hour for H100, $3.20 for H200, $5.00 for B200, and $8.00 for GB200 as of October 2026, while committed plans are discounted and storage and networking are priced separately.
- Utilization decides which model wins: Cast AI’s 2026 analysis of production clusters found average enterprise GPU utilization of roughly 5%, which shows how easily reserved capacity turns into paid idle time. Matching the pricing model to measured usage is the single biggest lever on GPU cost.

...

On GMI Cloud, all GPU resources are dedicated, single-tenant instances priced per GPU-hour, with the rate depending on GPU type and deployment model. Pay-as-you-go containers have no expiration date and can be terminated at any time, and pay-as-you-go managed clusters are charged by the minute with no upfront cost, as GMI explains in its guide to comparing container, bare metal, and managed cluster quotes.

results.title: Lyceum H100 went $2.79 to $3.49, GMI $2.00 to $2.60, October 7, 2026
highlights:
On October 7, 2026, two GPU clouds we read every hour printed higher H100 rates. In our read at 19:40:43 UTC, Lyceum’s price page listed an H100 80 GB on demand at $3.49 a GPU-hour, up from $2.79 an hour earlier, a rise of 25.1%. In our read at 08:40:55 UTC, GMI Cloud’s page listed its H100 “from” $2.60 a GPU-hour, up from $2.00, a rise of 30.0%. Neither page names the form factor, so both rates sit on our H100 80GB card, where the median rate card at 06:41 UTC on October 8 was $3.51 across 20 rate cards.

...

## GMI Cloud moved three “from” rates

GMI Cloud’s pricing page prints one figure per card as “from $X /GPU-hour”, an advertised starting rate, and our tables tag it that way. In the 08:40:55 UTC read on October 7, three of its four cards moved: H100 from $2.00 to $2.60, H200 from $2.60 to $3.20 (up 23.1%) and B200 from $4.00 to $5.00 (up 25.0%). GB200 stayed at $8.00. The read at 07:40:56 UTC still printed $2.00 for the H100, and the GMI module was not changed in that window. After the move, three of the 20 H100 rate cards on October 8 listed lower than GMI’s $2.60, and eight of the 43 H200 rate cards listed lower than its $3.20.

The Price Index is computed from the H100 SXM card only. Both rates here sit on the H100 80GB card, whose pages do not name a form factor, so neither move enters the index.

...

Every rate above was read from lyceum.technology/resources/pricing or gmicloud.ai/en/pricing at the minute named; both pages are public and print the dollar figure per GPU-hour as quoted here. /providers/lyceum and /providers/gmi-cloud list each current rate with the date it began standing, /changelog lists these moves, and /prices.json carries each row with its read time. results.title: B200 rental index hits record $8.54 per GPU-hour as CoreWeave slid: Orrn - Blockspace
results.author: William Foxley
highlights:
GPU data provider Ornn says its B200 GPU rental index hit a record of $8.54 per GPU-hour on Sunday, and its B300 index also set an all-time high, the compute exchange said Monday. Ornn said B200 rental prices rose 12.9% over the past trading week. Over the same week, shares of CoreWeave (NASDAQ: CRWV) fell 25.2%.

The B200 index eased 1.5% to $8.41 on Monday. It was still up 14.7% over seven days and 13.2% over 30 days. October’s average so far is $7.82, against $7.25 in September and $6.14 in August.

...

The index tracks only executed on-demand rentals, using a volume-weighted, winsorized mean over a rolling one-hour window. Reserved capacity, long-term agreements and forward contracts are excluded.

The index view is different. The Ornn Compute Price Index, reported in a post dated 27 April 2026 on tomtunguz.com, put the B200 at $4.95 per hour that week, up from $2.31 in early March, a 114% rise in six weeks. The author also reports that the B200 premium over H200 fell to $0.28 per hour in November 2025 and widened to $1.80 by late April 2026. That is one index, from one author, describing a spot style market, so its levels sit below most on-demand list prices. The takeaway is directional: Blackwell prices were rising in spring 2026, and the gap to the previous generation was widening.

results.title: Where to rent an H200 SXM at the cheapest price - GPUBank
results.author: GPUBank Research
highlights: Several specialised clouds sit between the cheap single-GPU offers and the large clouds. GMI Cloud's pricing page lists the H200 "from $3.20" per GPU-hour, marked available now, in its own data centres, without itemising what comes with it 20. Civo charges $3.49 for one H200 with 23 vCPU, 169 GB of RAM and 400 GB of NVMe, with free transfer but usage rounded up to the next full hour, and $2.99 on a 36-month commitment 14. Hyperstack lists $3.99 on demand and reserved capacity from $2.79, billed per minute with free traffic but public IPs charged separately 21. Hyperbolic shows $3.99, refreshed weekly from its suppliers' rates, and does not bill instances that fail to come online 17. DigitalOcean's H200 droplet costs $4.47 with 24 vCPU, 240 GiB of RAM, 5 TiB of scratch NVMe and 15,000 GiB of transfer, or $3.40 on a 12-month contract 22. GetDeploying listed further offers we could not read on the providers' own pages: Gcore at $3.56 per GPU for an 8x bare-metal node, Canopy Wave at $4.00 for two GPUs, Runcrate at $4.24 for one, and Crusoe at $5.40 and OVHcloud at $6.20 for 8-GPU machines; Together AI could not be resolved, with $5.99 for clusters in our September reading against a $2.99 row now labelled on demand, which matches its former spot price 6.
